title: Travelling vine shawl
subtitle: An asymmetric side-to-side shawl in fingering with a travelling vine lace panel.
excerpt: An asymmetric shawl in fingering-weight wool, worked side-to-side from one pointed tip to the other, with a 6-stitch travelling vine lace panel running along the growing upper edge. Wingspan approximately 180 cm, depth approximately 50 cm. About 320 g of fingering yarn.
sourceNotes: Travelling vine and leaf lace appears in multiple Victorian knitting references. The motif is documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 10th series (1895), §Lace Shawls, as a border stitch for triangular shawls. The side-to-side asymmetric construction is a modern application of the motif.

knitting.gaugeText: 24 sts × 48 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stockinette on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan approximately 180 cm. Depth approximately 50 cm at the deepest point. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A lace motif made up of yarn-over increases and matching decreases that create a diagonal line suggesting a climbing plant stem. The motif shifts one stitch to the left or right on each right-side row, creating movement across the fabric.

A length of smooth waste yarn threaded through all stitches on the needle at a given row. If a mistake is made past that point, the knitting can be ripped back to the lifeline row without losing any stitches.

content.text: An asymmetric side-to-side shawl in fingering-weight wool with a
travelling vine
lace panel along the upper edge. Wingspan approximately 180 cm, depth approximately 50 cm.

The asymmetric construction works from tip to tip: a 4-stitch cast-on grows on the upper edge by one stitch every RS row, while the lower edge remains a straight garter selvedge. The 6-stitch travelling vine panel sits against the upper selvedge and travels diagonally inward each RS row. Thread a
lifeline
every 100 rows. Budget about 320 g (about 1,280 m / 1,400 yards) of fingering wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 320 g (1,280 m / 1,400 yards) of fingering-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, 100 cm or longer

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 48 rows to 10 cm over stockinette on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. At gauge the 6-stitch vine panel measures about 2.5 cm wide. If your blocked gauge reads 26 stitches per 10 cm, the wingspan at the same row count will be about 166 cm. Work 12 extra RS rows to compensate, or change to 4 mm needles.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 4 stitches. Tail: allow approximately 20 cm. Work 4 plain garter rows. Place a marker after the first 3 stitches to mark the lower garter selvedge. Place a second marker 6 stitches from the first. The vine panel will occupy these 6 stitches once growth begins.
Body
RS row: k3 (garter selvedge), SM, work vine panel over 6 sts, SM, k to last st, yo, k1. (1 stitch added at upper edge)
WS row: k3, p to 3 sts from end, k3.

Vine panel (6 sts, RS rows): Row 1: k1, yo, k1, ssk, k2. Row 2 (WS): work WS as set. Row 3: k2, yo, k1, ssk, k1. Row 5: k3, yo, k1, ssk. Row 7: k2, k2tog, k1, yo, k1. Row 9: k1, k2tog, k1, yo, k2. Row 11: k2tog, k1, yo, k1, k1.
Continue until total wingspan reaches approximately 180 cm (approximately 432 RS rows at gauge, giving 4 + 432 = 436 stitches).
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off. A standard bind-off pulls the upper vine edge inward and prevents it from opening to full length.
Stitch count check-ins
After lifeline 1 (row 100): 4 + 100 = 104 stitches. Wingspan approximately 43 cm. The vine should show at least 8 complete repeat cycles.
After lifeline 4 (row 400): 404 stitches. Wingspan approximately 168 cm. The last 32 RS rows bring the shawl to the full 180 cm.
Common faults

Vine panel distorted: a yarn-over was dropped from the previous row instead of knitting it as a new stitch on the return WS row. Every yarn-over from a RS row creates a stitch on the WS row; the WS row must purl or knit across it.
Selvedge marker creeping into the vine panel: the lower garter selvedge marker was placed one stitch too far to the right. Recount 3 stitches from the cast-on end and reposition.
Blocking

Soak 15 minutes in cool water, press out in towels. Pin the lower straight edge first, then pin the two short tips. Pin the upper vine edge in a gentle curve opening out the lace. The vine definition improves dramatically after blocking.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. Re-block when the vine panel closes up after wearing.
What to try next
Mirror the vine panel: work a second 6-stitch vine along the lower selvedge in the opposite direction. The two vines travel away from each other, framing the entire body.
